Definition: a pasture (from its arrangement of the flock)
BiblicalUsage: A pasture, the place where the flock is arranged and fed, and Isaiah pictures the lambs feeding in their pasture after judgment has passed. The word also carries the sense of word or speaking, and Jeremiah's false prophets are called wind because their word is not in them. Micah promises to gather the remnant like sheep into a fold.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God is the shepherd who finds pasture for His flock even after judgment, and His word is what feeds them. The false prophet has wind; the true shepherd has a pasture.
